full_judgment:
Md Rezaul Hasan, J: On an application filed under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, this Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the impugned proceedings of GR Case No.400 of 2007, arising out of Badda PS Case No.12, dated 7-6-2007, under section 8(1) of the Natural Water Reservoir Conservation Act, .2000, read with section 384/430/431/447 of the Penal Code, pending before the Court of Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Court No. 1, Dhaka, should not be quashed and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. The prosecution case, in short, is that, one Salah Udd in, Inspector of Detective Branch, Dhaka Metropolitan Police, on 7-6-2007, lodged an FIR with Badda Police Station, against the this petitioner [who is the Chairman of Basundhara Group and Managing Director of East West Development (Pvt.) Limited] and three others, stating inter-alia that, they, in connivance with each other and in order to secure personal gain, have violated the provisions of section 5 of the Natural Water Reservoir Conservation Act, 2000, in the manner and during the period as alleged in the Ejhar and have forcefully occupied and grabbed property measuring 80.28 acres of land situated under Badda Police Station which was the Government property and thereby committed offence under section 384/430/431/ 447 of the Penal Code. 

 3. After investigation, the police has submitted two charge sheets in Badda Police Station Case No. 12 dated 7-6-2007, of which one being charge-sheet No. 24A dated 15-1-2008, under section 8(1) of the Natural Water Reservoir Conservation Act, 2000, read with section 384/430/431 /447 of the Penal Code and another under section 15(Kha)(1) of the Special Powers Act, 1974. 

 5. Learned Advocates Mr Ahsanul Karim, Mr Khairul Alam Chowdhury, Mr Aminul Hoque and Mr Muntaka Nusrat Khan appeared on behalf of the petitioner. Mr Karim, having placed the petition along with the supplementary affidavit and other documents annexed to the petition, points out at the outset that, in the FIR, there were two sets of allegations against this accused-petitioner, one is under section 8(1) of the Natural Water Reservoir Conservation Act, 2000 (the Act) and under section 384/430/431/447 of the Penal Code and another under section 15(Kha) (1) of the Special Powers Act, 1974. Then, referring to the provisions of section 12 of the Natural Water Reservoir Conservation Act, 2000, the learned Advocate first of all submits that, the impugned proceeding has been initiated on the basis of the FIR filed on 7-6-2007 by one Salah Uddin, Inspector of Detective Branch, Dhaka Metropolitan Police, which is evident from the FIR but the provisions of section 12(1) of the Act, stipulates that no court shall take cognizance of any offence under section of the Act, except upon a written complaint filed either by the Chairman or by any person specifically authorized by him in that behalf. He next points out that the word 'authority', for the purpose of the Act, has been defined in section 2(Ga) of the Act, that refers only to Rajdhani Unnayan Kartipokkho (RAJUK). He then submits that, on a mere perusal of the FIR and the charge-sheet, it will be evident that no written complaint was filed either by Chairman of RAJUK or by any person authorized by him, while the informant was not at all authorized by the Chairman of RAJUK to file any case against the petitioner, either by filing a complaint petition in the court or by lodging an FIR with Police Station. Moreso, he argues that this case has not been initiated upon a written complaint which is a mandatory requirement of law. Therefore, he proceeds on that, the informant had no authority to lodged the FIR and the trial court did not have any jurisdiction to take cognizance of any offences as per the police report No. 24A dated 15-1-2008 under this Act. Hence, he empathically argues, the impugned proceeding is without jurisdiction since its inception is absolutely an abuse of the process of the court and its initiation as well as its continuation is without jurisdiction. In support of his contention the learned Advocate has placed reliance on the decision reported in 15 BLC (AD) 191, in which the Appellate Division has upheld the judgment of the High Court Division by quashing the proceeding, since it was filed by an SI of Police without 

 permission of Bangladesh Bank and cognizance was taken by the Tribunal in violation of the provisions of section 23(2)(3) of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, that required prior sanction of Bangladesh Bank for filing a case and for taking cognizance under that Act, which was lacking in that case. He then submits that, the Natural Water Reservoir Conservation Act, 2000 is a special statute and section 3 of the Act makes it clear that this Act will supersede the provisions of other laws. Therefore, the informant had no authority to lodge the FIR and the trial court had no jurisdiction to take cognizance of the offence as alleged against the petitioner. He next argues that, further prolongation of this proceeding will cause serious hardship to the petitioner, while the reputation of the petitioner and his business has already been tarnished irreparably. He further submits that, this unauthorized FIR was filed on 7-6-2007, while in the FIR the date of occurrence has been shown from the year 1988 and the fact of this colossal delay in lodging the FIR has not at all been explained and that the impugned proceeding is absolutely malafide and is simply causing serious prejudice and harassment to the petitioner and that, on these grounds, the impugned proceeding is liable to be quashed. He next submits that, section 12(1) of the Act contemplates that it requires not only prior authorization, it further requires that the proceeding should be initiated on the basis of a complaint petition. The legislature has restricted the competence to file a complaint with a deliberate intent to prevent any abuse of this special law, arbitrarily or whimsically. Moreover, it is another safe-guard against the abuse that the proceeding must be initiated upon a complaint petition, not on the basis of an FIR to be made by the police. Hence, this proceeding is also liable to be quashed on these grounds, as well. The learned Advocate further submits that, even if the facts alleged in the FIR are taken to be true then also the same does not constitute any offence under section 384/430/431/447 of the Penal Code. The learned Advocate further submits that, on the self-same FIR another charge-sheet has been submitted in Metropolitan Special Tribunal Case No. 458 of 2008, arising out of Badda PS Case No.12(6)07, dated 7-6-2007, corresponding to GR No. 400 of 2007 under section 15(1)(Kha) of the Special Powers Act, 1974 and that proceeding was quashed by this Division on 2-2-2012 in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.10270 of 2007, vide the certified copy of the said judgment and order of the High Court Division, placed by the learned Advocate for the petitioner. He concludes that, the present proceeding against this petitioner is nothing but a serious harassment and a clear abuse of the process of the court, hence it is liable to be quashed. 

 6. Learned Deputy Attorney-General Mr Md Giasuddin Ahammed, appearing on behalf of the opposite party-State submits that, this FIR has been lodged since authorized by the Gurutoro Aporadh Daman Somonnoy Committee, Dhaka, against this petitioner and others. As such, the informant was authorized by that authority. So, he maintains that there is no lack of authority. Then he submits that, the requirement of section 12(1) of the Act is not conclusive and the court has jurisdiction to take cognizance of the offence as per FIR filed by police. Therefore, the question of authority in lodging the FIR is a mere technical ground. The learned DAG proceeds on that, the provisions of section 12 of the Act requiring authority from RAJUK in this case or requiring filing this case is not mandatory in as much as no consequence for violation of section 12 has been mentioned. In support of his contention, the learned DAG has cited a decision reported in 13 BLC 237: between SM Mozammel Hogue Talukder vs State, later on affirmed by the Appellate Division in Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 53 of 2008. He proceeds on that the grounds taken in the petition filed under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure are all questions of fact and it can be decided only by adducing evidence in the trial court. He concludes that this Rule has no merit and the same is liable to be discharged. 

 11. As such, in order to legally initiate a proceeding under section 12(1) of the Act, two pre-conditions shall have to be fulfilled, namely (1) a complaint has to be filed in writing and (2) it has to be filed, either by the Chairman, RAJUK, or by any person authorized by him. Therefore, we have to examine as to whether these two pre-conditions were fulfilled or not in this case. 

 13. Besides, no complaint in writing was filed against this petitioner, as required by law. The difference between a complaint petition and an FIRs is not one of mere form, rather it is one of great legal substance. An FIR is filed with the police, under section 154 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, whereas a complaint petition has to be filed before the designated Court and the procedure laid down in section 200 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, is to be followed (unless a deferent procedure is laid down in the concerned statute). The law lays down a totally different procedure to be followed in respect of a complaint case, as distinct from a GR case that arises from an Ejhar. 

 14. The intention of the legislature to provide a safeguard, against any arbitrary exercise of power under section 12(1) of the Act, is clear in stipulating that none other than the CEO/Chairman or a person authorized by him can only file a complaint and that the complaint must be in writing. But, none of these mandatory requirements of law was complied with, in this case, as we have already taken notice of. 

 “আপাততঃ বলবৎ অন্য কোন আইনে যাহা কিছুই থাকুক না কেন, এই আইন ও তদধীনে প্রণীত বিধির বিধানাবলী কার্যকর থাকিবে ।”Hence, this being a special law, its provisions shall supersede and prevail over all other laws including section 154, 173 and 200 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, in the matter of entertaining a case and investigation." 

 16. The decision reported in 13 BLC 237 deals with an issue of interpretation of statute, which is not before us. Here the issue is about the lack of competence to file the case. Hence, the decision reported in 44 DLR (AD) 260 : Rupali Bank vs Tafazzal Hossain is relevant here, wherein it has been held by the apex court that— 

 17. Therefore, we have no hesitation to hold that, the impugned proceeding has been initiated by an unauthorized person, in clear violation of section 12(1) of the Act, and the cognizance taken by the court on the basis of police report No. 24A dated 15-1-2008 of Badda Police Station is clearly beyond its competence. In this case the judgment passed by the Appellate Division in the case of 15 BLC (AD) 191 applies with full force. 

 18. Section 384/430/431/447 of the Penal Code deals with punishment for extortion, mischief and punishment for criminal trespass. No ingredient of these offences has been found in the contents of the FIR or in the these police report. These allegations, made long after 1988 without even giving any reason for the delay, does not constitute any offence under the aforesaid sections, even if these are assumed to be true. These are preposterous. 

 19. The date of occurrence is shown since 1988, while this case has been filed in the year 2007, without any explanation about the cause of delay. The fact that there is no limitation in filing a criminal case should not be granted as an open-ended licence to abuse the process of the courts. Hence, apparently this unexplained long delay, coupled with lack of competence to initiate the questioned proceeding, renders it a clear abuse of the process of the Court. 

 20. Moreso, on the self-same FIR, another proceeding has already been quashed by this Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.10270 of 2007 dated 2-2-2012. Therefore, this is one of the similar multiple proceedings and is a glaring instance of an abuse of the process of the Courts. 

 21. The learned DAG prayed for adjournment of the hearing in order to produce Case Diary (CD). Though we should dispose of this Rule solely on the basis of the statements made in the FIR and the Police Report, however, as an exception to the usual practice and procedure, we have allowed adjournment. Accordingly, the learned DAG placed the CD Having examined the CD and the minutes placed therewith, we find that no authority was given to the informant to file this case, as we have recorded herein before from our perusal of the FIR and the police report. 

 22. Though not imperative for disposal of this Rule, it may, however, be pertinent to record that, many criminal cases are filed not to seek justice or to ensure the rule of law. Instances of false or frivolous cases filed with or by the police or in criminal courts are not rare. The courts and the police should not be allowed to be used by a section of unscrupulous people as if these are post offices. They should not be used as apparatus to oppress or harass any one's target. The Court must adhere to its role as referee in between the prosecution and the accused persons and must dispassionately perform its functions without letting the cries, clamors, rage or emotion of the audience or of the gallery to influence it. 

 23. Abuse of the process of the court seems to have reached an alarming stage that has been causing serious hardship, mental agony, stress and sufferings as well as reputational loss to the citizens who were not otherwise liable to be treated as such, but for the system that indulges malicious prosecution for having no easy and practical remedy available against the same. Many of such cases were filed during 2007-2008 regime. This type of unauthorized proceedings should be buried in limine, as the citizens are entitled to be treated in accordance with law. 

 The impugned proceedings of GR Case No.400 of 2007 arising out of Badda PS Case No.12 dated 7-6-2007 under section 8(1) of the Natural Water Reservoir Conservation Act, 2000 read with section 384/430/431/447 of the Penal Code, pending before the Court of Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Court No. 1, Dhaka, is hereby quashed.
